📄 Iran, Pakistan close to finalizing free trade agreement: Official

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The deputy director of the East Asia and Subcontinent Office at the Iran Trade Promotion Organization says Iran’s trade with Pakistan is ongoing, and the two countries’ free trade agreement is in its final stages and is expected to be finalized by the end of this year.

In an exclusive interview with IRNA on Saturday, Mehrdad Siyadat-Nasab said the Iran-Pakistan free trade agreement has reached its final stages, adding that its implementation could boost bilateral trade by reducing customs costs.
​
He put Iran-Pakistan formal and informal trade at around $6 billion, saying it could exceed $10 billion given the existing economic potential.
​
Siyadat-Nasab said petrochemical products, liquefied gas, steel, tiles, and ceramics are Iran’s key export capacities to Pakistan, stressing the need to expand cooperation in industrial, agricultural, mining, and technical and engineering sectors.
​
He also highlighted the use of Pakistan’s port capacities, market knowledge, private-sector engagement, and development of logistical infrastructure as key factors in expanding bilateral trade.
